utterances.text: Later on that evening -- that afternoon, there were Dutch F-16 fighters who were attacking one or two tanks that were in my neighbour, that were threatening me, and they carried out well. The tanks disappeared; I don't know whether they were hit. But I could go back to the city of Srebrenica to help Captain Groen with his Bravo Company. So there was a close air support with two F-16s in the afternoon, instead of a gunship promised by us in the morning, the early morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: When you say "the afternoon," do you know which date that was?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: What's the date? Sorry?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Which date?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: It was the 11th.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, you said you returned to Srebrenica town. What did you see and what did you do then?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: Well, there were thousands of people looking at you and asking -- they asked me, "What should I do?" and we tried to move all those people to Potocari because we were certain that the Bosnian Serbs would attack the town real soon. And that's when I told my soldiers to leave the APC, and I got as many wounded and mentally ill people as possible on my APC, and I drove in front of them towards Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: When you say you drove in front of "them," who are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: I'm referring to the refugees. I'm not in front of them, I'm driving between them. They are coming with me towards Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Where were you in relation to the column of refugees that were going from Srebrenica to Potocari? What was your position?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: About one kilometre behind them. So I'm not at the front but I'm nearly at the front.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Were you the first of the UN armoured vehicles in that column?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: One of the first, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: When you were advancing toward Potocari with a column, did you see or hear any artillery fire in and around the advancing column toward Potocari?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: I did. I saw some Bosnian Serb artillery to the left and right of the road. All the refugees took to Potocari. I thought they wanted to scare them and wanted to impress them. They didn't hit the road but nearby the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I'm reminded by my colleague that we have to slow down. So since we speak the same language, if you would pause after I ask a question and I will pause after you answer a question before I give you my next question, then the interpreters would be greatly assisted in their job. We've talked about this before. Let me return to the examination, then. Where was the shelling hitting in respect of the column? And could you tell the type of artillery or weapons used in the shelling?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: I saw some detonations about 100 metres from the road the refugees took. I couldn't see whether it was mortar fire or if it was artillery, but it definitely was one of those two.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. What result did that firing of the artillery have on the people in the column of refugees?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: The refugees were very scared, of course. And they saw two F-16s coming over the town to support them, support us, and when they saw the Bosnian Serbs shelling them again, in the nearance [sic] of the road, they were very, very scared, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, did you eventually succeed in getting to Potocari on the 11th of July?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: I did, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: What did you do that night?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: When I arrived at Potocari, I took care of all the ill people who were in my APC, and then after four days of blocking position, I took 12 hours off. I slept.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: So you had been up for four days, the previous four days; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: Correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. Let me turn your attention, then, to the next day after you woke up, which would be the 12th of July. Did you receive any orders from Major Franken that morning?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: What were those orders?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: I had to assemble 12 soldiers and meet him at a conference room.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And what were your orders then?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: My orders then were to escort the buses who were appearing nearby the main gate, and take some food, take some water, take a sleeping bag. "We don't know where the buses are going to; we don't know where you're going to. Stay by the buses and try to radio everything you see on your way." That was my order.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And who was in the buses?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: In the buses were the women and children, the refugees, the Muslims, who were gathered by the HQ of DutchBat.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Did any other Dutch officers accompany you on your escort duty on this occasion?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: I escorted the first convoy of the deportation, and in front of this row of buses there was another UN vehicle, with Major Boering and a captain, and I was at the end of the convoy.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, I'd like you to describe your journey on that first convoy that left Potocari, and I would like you to, first of all, tell the Judges about what you observed in the town of Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: When you leave OP Papa, it's the northern part of the enclave, soon you will be on a road going through Bratunac, and there were Bosnian Serbs, hundreds of them, standing on both sides of the road, partying, celebrating, shouting, throwing things at the buses. I was very, very scared. It reminded me of a video movie we saw a few weeks before called "Schindler's List", and you see there the Jews walking towards trains and a lot of other people standing nearby the road and shouting at them as well. It was the same picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Did you succeed in -- you succeeded eventually in getting through Bratunac, did you not?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: Yes, I did, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Did something happen to one of the buses in the convoy that you were escorting?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: One of the buses, the engine caught on fire. It stopped on the right side of the road. And all the other buses passed this bus and were following the leading bus towards Kladanj. And I stopped nearby this road, I stopped with this bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: What happened?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: There were several Bosnian Serbs coming towards the refugees who were in the bus. I ordered them all out of the bus. I wanted them to be safe because there was a fire in the engine. At that time I handed them over all my food, all my medicine, and all the water I had, because they were very thirsty, very hungry, and very scared, with a lot of headaches of course. Then I ordered them -- I allowed them to go to a river nearby and drink, and I saw a lot of Bosnian Serbs coming towards this group of people, just standing there looking at them. Then a few Bosnian Serb soldiers approached with a photo camera, with some cans of lemonade, and they were giving them to the children and taking pictures of it, for propaganda use.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Did the bus eventually -- was it eventually repaired and could it continue on its journey?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: It could not continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Was another bus brought to bring those refugees on their route?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: The bus driver asked to borrow my Mercedes, UN, to get another bus, but I told him to solve -- to let himself solve this problem. And he managed to get another bus. So there was another bus that the refugees got in, and I followed that bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Which direction did you take? Could you use Prosecutor's Exhibit 1E, which is to your right, and take the pointer and just indicate on this large exhibit the route which you travelled with that bus.

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: I'll talk louder. This is the city of Bratunac [indicates]. So we left from Potocari to Bratunac, towards Konjevic Polje. Here [indicates] we go to the south, crossing Nova Kasaba, Milici, Lazenica [phoen], and heading for Kladanj.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, can you point -- use your pointer and as best as you can recall, where did that bus break down?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: The bus broke down in this location here [indicates].

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: For the record, the witness has indicated the area on the right and the left side of the town of Glogova.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, as you -- you can have a seat, Captain Egbers. Thank you. Captain Egbers, as you advanced, then, on your journey, what did you see?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: I saw a lot of infantry -- Bosnian Serb infantry on the road, facing the woods, facing the enclave, and firing at the woods. And they told me there were Muslim fighters in the woods and they would fire on them. So they stopped me -- they would fire an anti-aircraft gun at the woods with great rockets, and then when they got finished, the bus and I could go through.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Did you hear any return fire from the woods in the direction of the Bosnian Serbs?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: No, sir, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: How many soldiers would you estimate you saw in the stretch between, say, Sandici and Nova Kasaba?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: Well, I saw hundreds of them grouping with, let's say, five or six together, and then 20 metres on, another group, always facing the woods, nearby -- between Sandici, Nova Kasaba, and Milici.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: How were they dressed?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: They were dressed in green. They were Bosnian Serb infantry. They were well-armed with AK-47s, with machine-guns, and they had vehicles with anti-aircraft guns on it, with four barrels, firing at the woods.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Did you have an occasion to pass a football field near Nova Kasaba on your journey toward the drop-off point with that bus?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Let me show you Prosecutor's -- I'm going to show you two exhibits.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: So if the usher can be given two exhibits, Prosecutor's Exhibit 12/4, which I should like placed on the ELMO first, and then Prosecutor's Exhibit 12/2. So, Mr. Usher, if we could start by placing 12/4 on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Have you seen this picture before, Captain Egbers?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: This is the football field nearby Nova Kasaba.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, could you describe to the Judges what you saw at that location on the 12th of July?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: When you drive the car over the road, you see -- you can look through the trees, and I saw this field covered with men, sitting on their knees with their hands on their necks. There was a table on which there were some soldiers, and there were some soldiers around the football field.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: How many people were there on their knees, with their hands behind their neck?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: Almost the entire football field was covered with men.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now let me show you Prosecutor's Exhibit 12/2. Now, this is an aerial image, Captain Egbers, and it is dated the 13th of July, 1995, at approximately 1400 hours. And you will see indicated on the football pitch two ovals and some dark markings within those ovals, which those have been identified as groups of prisoners. Were there more prisoners that you saw on the football pitch than are indicated in Prosecutor's Exhibit 12/2?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: Yes, sir. I saw the entire football field covered with men.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: There must have been hundreds of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Did you see any -- let me withdraw that question. Were you able to ascertain who those men were?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: Well, when I drove over this road, towards Nova Kasaba, I saw some groups of Muslims walking towards the football field with their hands on their necks, and those were the Muslim men who were taken from the woods.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, eventually, Captain Egbers, did you arrive at a destination where the bus stopped and people on the buses were discharged?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: I did, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Do you know where that location was?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: It was in the nearance [sic] of Kladanj, near the confrontation line.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Did anything unusual happen there, at that location, at that time?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: It was well organised. The buses stopped there. The women and children saw me and they made this sign [indicates] to me, so they were sure they would be killed, because it was in the middle of the woods and all those buses stopped over there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: When you say "this sign," you indicated, for the record, your finger went from your right shoulder to your left shoulder, across your neck.

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: That's right, sir. They were certain that the journey stopped there for them and that they would be slaughtered. Then I saw three of those buses drive through a point where they could debark, the refugees could get out of the bus, and had to walk towards the road, towards central Bosnia. And when those three buses were empty, another three buses had to drive on. So it was well organised, and in the first convoy, a lot of women and children walked a few miles towards central Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Excuse me. I just want to know what he means by "central Bosnia". To the woods? To the city? What?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: What do you mean by "central Bosnia"? In which direction were they walking?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: They were walking in a western direction, near the confrontation line, in the direction of Kladanj. We were stopped not nearby by the city, but in between -- in the woods. So there was a lot of wood on the left and right of the road, so that's why the women thought that their lives would end there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, you returned to Potocari after that debarkation was concluded?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: I did, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Did you pass that football field that you previously testified about, that is, the football field near Nova Kasaba?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: I did, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: What did you see at the football field when you returned?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: I saw that it was covered with a hundreds of men with their hands still on their necks, on their knees.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: So a scene that was very much similar to what you had seen when you passed by the first time?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: It was, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, let me focus your attention to the 13th of July. You have returned to Potocari. Did you receive an assignment on the 13th of July?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: There was a captain who ordered me to report at 0600 to escort another convoy, but my convoy, it was convoy number 4, it wouldn't leave until 11.00. So between 6.00 and 11.00, I was in the surrounding of the main gate.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Did you have an occasion to see anything occurring at a location known as the White House?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: I saw -- yes, I did, sir. I saw and I heard a woman screaming for help, and I reacted on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Why was she screaming?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: She was screaming because she had to enter the buses, and her man or the male had to stay in the White House. He was brought there by Bosnian Serb infantry soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Let me just very quickly have you identify the White House.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And if I could Prosecutor's Exhibit 5/17 placed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you if you can identify this structure in this exhibit as the White House. Do you see Prosecutor's Exhibit 5/17 that's been placed on the ELMO?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: I can see it sir. That's the same house.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: That's the White House that's in the centre, off to the right of this particular exhibit; is that right, sir?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: After you heard the screaming of the woman, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: I contacted two corporals who was standing near the White House and I asked them what was going on. They told me they didn't know because they were not allowed to enter the White House. When I asked them, "Why aren't you allowed?" Well, the Bosnian Serbs wouldn't let them. That's when I approached these Bosnian Serb soldiers and I told them that I was a First Lieutenant and that I wanted to inspect the White House, and I went in.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: How were the Bosnian Serb soldiers who were around the White House dressed; do you remember?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: They were dressed in green, green camouflage, infantry uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: What happened when you went?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: I saw men sitting in different rooms, just waiting for things to happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Did you have a conversation with any of the Bosnian Serb soldiers who were there?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: I did. I asked them, "Why would you separate the men from the women," and he pointed at a lot of knives, just pocket knives that were lying there and said, "Well, you see, they are all armed with knives and we don't want them to attack one of our bus drivers."

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Did they say anything else?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: They told me later on that they would bring them to Kladanj.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: So the Bosnian Serb soldiers told you they would bring them to Kladanj.

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: They did, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Did you see anything else in addition to the pocket knives?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: I saw some money from former Yugoslavia. I saw some pictures of families. A lot of luggage left there by the men.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Where did you see the photos of the families, the luggage, and the money?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: In the garden of the town -- of the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: In front of the White House? On the side of the White House?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: In front and -- in front of the White House.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right. Now, did you see any buses with men from the White House -- I'm sorry. Did you see any men from the White House board buses?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: I did, sir. There were three buses loaded with men, and it had a number 3. It was escorted by my colleague who had to escort number 3, I had to escort number 4. I was there and I told them that the Bosnian Serbs would bring them to Kladanj, but the men told me otherwise. They said no, and they made the same signal I just described, the same signal. "They will kill them," that's what they said, and they offered me some German marks.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Could you just demonstrate for the Chamber the signal that was made to you by at least one or maybe more of the Muslim men you saw within the White House?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: It was this signal, sir [indicates].

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Again, the record should reflect the finger crossing the neck from the left shoulder to the right shoulder.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, you say they offered you some Deutschemarks. Who offered you the Deutschemarks?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: The Muslim men, because they said that it was useless to them. I then believed that they would go to Kladanj, they would be escorted. And I said, "No, keep the money. It's your money. I don't want it."

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: How many men did you see get into the buses, or approximately how many men did you see?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: Nearly 200.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: How did those men look when they were getting on those buses?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: They were very scared. They were mostly elder men. Scared, very scared, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: We have to slow down once again, I believe, I'm reminded by my colleague. Did you ever see any Muslim men walking in the direction of the White House under Bosnian Serb army escort?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: I saw one man with his hands on his neck, being taken to the White House by a Bosnian Serb.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, is there anything else you can tell us about the White House that you recall, or have you told us everything you know about the White House, as you remember it today?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: Everything, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right. Do you know what happened to the convoy of three buses that you saw leave with the men?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: I left with convoy number 4 later on, but some days later, I've been told, those three buses never left Bratunac. They went to Bratunac and the escort was stopped there by the Bosnian Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Let me ask you, then, you proceeded then with your convoy; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Did you take the same route that you had taken the day before?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: I did, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: How many buses were -- approximately how many buses were in the convoy that you were escorting?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: About 14 or 15.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, what did you see that struck you as significant while you were making your journey toward your ultimate destination, near Kladanj?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: We were stopped several times. There were AK-47s pointed at our heads, and we had to hand over our armoured vest, our helmets, and everything they wanted from the car. It happened about seven times that journey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Did you refuse -- apparently you must have refused about six times; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: I did. I pointed at my rank and I translated that into their language and told the Bosnian Serbs that I was a First Lieutenant and that I needed it myself, and we drove on.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Ultimately did you relinquish your body armour, and did your driver as well relinquish his body armour and his helmet?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: Yes, sir, but that was when there was an AK-47 at our heads.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: So the items that you relinquished were relinquished under force.

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: They were, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. Now, could you describe -- did you see any soldiers in the area as you were proceeding toward Kladanj, Bosnian Serb soldiers?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: I saw, from Sandici until Nova Kasaba, every three metres, a few soldiers. So there were a lot more soldiers. They were dressed in green, not as disciplined as the troops who were there the first day. They were heavily armed, firing at the woods where the Muslim men were supposed to be. And they were regular soldiers but not as disciplined.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, at least on this part of the journey, did you hear any firing coming out of the woods in the direction of those soldiers?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: No, sir, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Did you pass the football pitch again at Nova Kasaba?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And the same field that you've identified earlier in an exhibit; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: It's the same field.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: What did you see at that football field, on the 13th of July, as you made your way toward Kladanj?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: It was still covered with men, sitting on their knees, with their hands on their neck.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Were there fewer men on their knees? Were there the same amount of men? Were there more? How would you describe the number of men on their knees that you saw at Nova Kasaba football field?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: The same amount.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Did these appear to be Bosnian Muslim men who had been taken from the woods?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: Yes, sir, because there were groups of Muslims walking, with their hands on their neck, towards the football field.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Who was surrounding these men at the football pitch?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: I'm not sure. But I saw a truck with a white wolf's head painted on the doors of the truck. It was a crying wolf. And later on the Bosnian Serbs told me that it was a truck of the Drina Wolves.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, perhaps --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Are we going to conclude, Judge Riad, at 2.30?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: How long do you have to go?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I have a considerable time to go.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: So if you have to finish one question, we can conclude after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Well, did you proceed, then, on your journey to Kladanj, after you passed the football pitch?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Judge Riad, I have a number -- Captain Egbers has a number of other observations on this particular leg of his journey that he will be describing in his testimony, but this would be an appropriate place to stop.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: If it is appropriate for you, it is appropriate for us. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Captain Egbers, we will request you coming tomorrow, at 9.30.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: So we'll adjourn until tomorrow, at 9.30. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
